Suggested Lead:~ ""Y.M.C.A. RAISES LARGEST SUM IN IT'S HISTORY" 

As he thanked workers at the official closing luncheon today, 
lin Robert H.Hoope, the 1965 Campaign Chairman said "Today's total of 
{283,67 is the most money the Montreal "Y" has ever raised in a Campaign 
for operating assistance, and your zreat work is almost complete, 
We are now 422.579 ahead of this point in the last comparable campaign. 
By having the balance of approximately $26,000, now in the hands of a 
celatively small number of canvassers and subscribers, turned in by 
next week, we will have achieved the three goals we set ourselves - 
(1) To raise ‘310,000 (2) To do it in the shortest time on record, and 
(3) to make friends for the Y.M.C.A," 
Tn congratulating Mr.Hoppe and his workers, Mr.H.Roy Crabtree, President, 
noted that the remaining balance was critical for the full effectiveness 
of all the operations across the City of Montreal in the coming year. 
Mr.Fred Hubbard, the Y's General Secretary, pointed out that where 
people understand the Y's story they respond. ‘Corporations are comprised of 
people, newspapers are written by people, radio and televisions programs are 
produced by people - all of whom feel a social responsibility. In their support 


of this Campaign they have certainly proved that they exercise that responsibility!

In lauding the campaign workers, Mr.Hubbard stated his conviction 
that "This organisation, this web of human relationships, has come to 
feel strongly about developing and maturing the fundamentals of individual 
andcoorporate responsibility for the common good in this area of greater 
Montreal" 
Given recognition for outstanding work were:- R.Gordon James, Walter H.Palmer, 
G.Lloyd Welton and John P.Moynaugh. 


Northmount and Westmount Divisions have exceeded their campaign objectives.
